raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

When a serving engine is host-bound, one stray host-device sync in the scheduler path (an `.item()`, a `.tolist()` of a device tensor, a pageable `torch.tensor(..., device="cuda")`) makes the host wait for the GPU queue to drain, so it can no longer launch ahead. The scheduler already exports wall time per stage (`sglang:scheduler_stage_seconds_total`, #37636, #42025), but nothing says **where** the host blocks or **how often per step**. torch's sync debug mode can report every sync, but its warnings are deduplicated per location and carry no step context, so they cannot answer "how many syncs does one decode step or one extend cost, and from which call sites?"

This PR adds an opt-in census: with `SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_TARGET` set, the scheduler counts every sync torch reports under the scheduler stage it ran in, the forward mode of the batch being launched or processed, and its Python call site. It writes one JSON record per interval, together with the number of launched batches per forward mode. Syncs per decode step or per extend then follow by division.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/utils/scheduler_host_sync_logger.py` (new): `SchedulerHostSyncLogger`. On the first launched batch it calls `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")`, adds an `"always"` filter for the sync warning, and installs a `warnings.showwarning` hook that counts each sync under `(stage, forward_mode, call_site)`. The call site is the three innermost frames outside torch and `warnings`. Every `SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_INTERVAL` seconds it writes a `scheduler.host_syncs` record through `log_json`, using the same targets as `SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_STATUS_TARGET` (`stdout` or a directory with one file per host and rank).
- `observability/scheduler_stage_metrics.py`: a read-only `current_stage` property on the existing recorder. Stages come from that recorder, so the logger needs `--enable-metrics` and raises a clear error otherwise, as the status logger does.
- `managers/scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py`: creates the logger next to the scheduler status logger.
- `managers/scheduler.py`: two hooks, at `_on_step_launch` (inside `run_batch`) and at the top of `process_batch_result`. When the variable is unset each costs one attribute check per batch.
- `environ.py` + `docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`: `SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_TARGET` (default `""`, off) and `SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_INTERVAL` (default `60.0`), in the Logging section.
- Tests: `test/registered/unit/observability/test_scheduler_host_sync_logger.py` (new, `1-gpu-small`). It covers enable/disable, attribution by stage, mode and call site, window reset, pass-through of other warnings, the warning when the hook is replaced, one real `.item()` on CUDA, and that the scheduler's `_on_step_launch` and `process_batch_result` call the logger's hooks once per step. Two scheduler test doubles gain the new attribute.

Limits: only syncs that torch's sync debug mode reports are counted. Explicit `torch.cuda.synchronize()` and event waits such as the result `copy_done` are not counted. The mode is process-wide, so syncs from helper threads are counted too, under the scheduler's current stage; the counter is not locked, so a sync on a helper thread that races the scheduler thread's count can be lost. The sync debug mode, the warning filter and the `showwarning` hook are process-global and stay installed for the life of the process. If another component later replaces `warnings.showwarning`, the logger logs one warning, because syncs are no longer counted from then on.

Example record (abridged):

```json
{"event": "scheduler.host_syncs", "rank": 0, "window_s": 10.09, "launched_batches": {"extend": 15},
 "total_syncs": 188, "syncs": [{"stage": "run_batch", "forward_mode": "extend",
   "call_site": "srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py:673 _metadata_from_forward_batch <- ...", "count": 30}, ...]}
```

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change: the logger only observes.

| GPU | Model | Server args | Prompts | Logger on vs upstream main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q | `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` | `--enable-deterministic-inference --enable-metrics` | 4 greedy prompts: single, repeated, and as one batch of 4 | byte-identical output JSON; the logger wrote `scheduler.host_syncs` records during the run |
| GB300 | same | same | same | byte-identical (main and branch ran as consecutive jobs on two GB300 nodes) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Off by default. When off, the only cost is one attribute check per launched batch and one per processed batch. When on, it is a debugging mode: each reported sync walks a few Python frames.

What it shows on upstream main (`8d4e1ce4c7`), serving Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 (RTX: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`; GB300: `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`) with NEXTN MTP (3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens) at TP 1:

| GPU | Decode steps | Host syncs per decode step | Syncs per extend (no prefix) | Syncs per extend (prefix-cache hit) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q, `--quantization modelopt_fp4 --ple-offload-embedding --mem-fraction-static 0.93 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 4096` | 11,411 | 0 | 11.35 | 26.4 |
| GB300, defaults | 1,691 | 0 | 11.7 | 32.2 |

All counted syncs sit in `run_batch` for extend batches. The top call sites are an unsized `repeat_interleave` in the QSA extend metadata (4 per extend), per-layer QSA length uploads on prefix extends, and FLA chunk-index readbacks at the first GDN layer (3 per extend). Workloads: `sglang.benchmark.serving` random-ids 256/1024 at concurrency 16 (decode), random-ids 2048/1 at concurrency 4 (extend), and generated-shared-prefix 8×8 with a 4096-token system prompt over 2 turns (prefix).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`pre-commit run --all-files` clean.)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`test/registered/unit/observability/test_scheduler_host_sync_logger.py`.)
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (`environment_variables.mdx`.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (No output change; off-path cost is one attribute check per batch.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Prepared with the help of Claude Code; every result above was measured as described.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -0,0 +1,179 @@
+"""Count host-device syncs in the scheduler process by stage and call site.
+
+With ``SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_TARGET`` set, the scheduler turns on
+``torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")`` at its first batch and counts every
+synchronizing CUDA operation torch reports (``item()``, ``tolist()``,
+``nonzero``, pageable host-to-device copies, ...) under the scheduler stage it
+ran in, the forward mode of the batch being launched or processed, and its
+Python call site. Every ``SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_INTERVAL`` seconds a
+``scheduler.host_syncs`` JSON record with these counts and the number of
+launched batches per forward mode goes to each target, so syncs per decode step
+or per extend follow by division. Explicit ``torch.cuda.synchronize()`` and
+event waits are not reported by torch's sync debug mode and are not counted.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import os
+import sys
+import time
+import warnings
+from collections import Counter
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, List, Optional
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.observability.scheduler_stage_metrics import (
+    SCHEDULER_STAGE_PROCESS_BATCH_RESULT,
+    SCHEDULER_STAGE_RUN_BATCH,
+    SchedulerStageMetricsRecorder,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils.log_utils import create_log_targets, log_json
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import ScheduleBatch
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_SYNC_WARNING = "called a synchronizing CUDA operation"
+_TORCH_DIR = os.path.dirname(torch.__file__) + os.sep
+_SGLANG_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(__file__))) + os.sep
+_BATCH_STAGES = (SCHEDULER_STAGE_RUN_BATCH, SCHEDULER_STAGE_PROCESS_BATCH_RESULT)
+_CALL_SITE_DEPTH = 3
+_MAX_CALL_SITES = 100
+
+
+def _call_site(frame, depth: int = _CALL_SITE_DEPTH) -> str:
+    """The innermost ``depth`` frames outside torch and warnings, innermost first."""
+    parts = []
+    while frame is not None and len(parts) < depth:
+        filename = frame.f_code.co_filename
+        if not (
+            filename.startswith(_TORCH_DIR)
+            or filename.endswith("warnings.py")
+            or filename == __file__
+        ):
+            if filename.startswith(_SGLANG_DIR):
+                filename = filename[len(_SGLANG_DIR) :]
+            parts.append(f"{filename}:{frame.f_lineno} {frame.f_code.co_name}")
+        frame = frame.f_back
+    return " <- ".join(parts)
+
+
+class SchedulerHostSyncLogger:
+    """Process-global and never restored: the first launched batch sets torch's
+    sync debug mode, adds a warnings filter and replaces ``warnings.showwarning``
+    for the rest of the process."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        targets: List[str],
+        dump_interval: float,
+        stage_recorder: SchedulerStageMetricsRecorder,
+    ):
+        self.loggers = create_log_targets(targets=targets, name_prefix=__name__)
+        self.dump_interval = dump_interval
+        self.rank = dist.get_rank() if dist.is_initialized() else 0
+        self._stage_recorder = stage_recorder
+        self._forward_mode = ""
+        self._syncs: Counter = Counter()
+        self._launched_batches: Counter = Counter()
+        self._started = False
+        self._show = None
+        self._hook_replaced = False
+        self._last_dump_time = time.monotonic()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def maybe_create(
+        enable_metrics: bool, stage_recorder: SchedulerStageMetricsRecorder
+    ) -> Optional[SchedulerHostSyncLogger]:
+        target = envs.SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_TARGET.get()
+        if not target:
+            return None
+
+        if not enable_metrics:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_TARGET is set but --enable-metrics "
+                "is not active. Host-sync logging attributes syncs to scheduler "
+                "stages, which require --enable-metrics."
+            )
+
+        return SchedulerHostSyncLogger(
+            targets=[t.strip() for t in target.split(",") if t.strip()],
+            dump_interval=envs.SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_INTERVAL.get(),
+            stage_recorder=stage_recorder,
+        )
+
+    def on_step_launch(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> None:
+        if not self._started:
+            self._start()
+        self._maybe_dump()
+        self._forward_mode = batch.forward_mode.name.lower()
+        self._launched_batches[self._forward_mode] += 1
+
+    def on_step_result(self, batch: ScheduleBatch) -> None:
+        self._forward_mode = batch.forward_mode.name.lower()
+
+    def _start(self) -> None:
+        # "warn" rather than "error": an error could be swallowed by a broad
+        # except in the scheduler, a warning always reaches this hook
+        self._started = True
+        warnings.filterwarnings("always", message=_SYNC_WARNING)
+        show_other = warnings.showwarning
+
+        def show(message, category, filename, lineno, file=None, line=None):
+            if _SYNC_WARNING in str(message):
+                self._record(_call_site(sys._getframe(1)))
+            else:
+                show_other(message, category, filename, lineno, file, line)
+
+        self._show = show
+        warnings.showwarning = show
+        torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")
+
+    def _record(self, call_site: str) -> None:
+        stage = self._stage_recorder.current_stage
+        forward_mode = self._forward_mode if stage in _BATCH_STAGES else ""
+        self._syncs[stage, forward_mode, call_site] += 1
+
+    def _maybe_dump(self) -> None:
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        if now - self._last_dump_time < self.dump_interval:
+            return
+        if warnings.showwarning is not self._show and not self._hook_replaced:
+            self._hook_replaced = True
+            logger.warning(
+                "warnings.showwarning was replaced after host-sync logging "
+                "started; host syncs are no longer counted."
+            )
+        if not self._syncs and not self._launched_batches:
+            self._last_dump_time = now
+            return
+
+        log_json(
+            self.loggers,
+            "scheduler.host_syncs",
+            {
+                "rank": self.rank,
+                "window_s": round(now - self._last_dump_time, 3),
+                "launched_batches": dict(self._launched_batches),
+                "total_syncs": sum(self._syncs.values()),
+                "syncs": [
+                    {
+                        "stage": stage,
+                        "forward_mode": forward_mode,
+                        "call_site": call_site,
+                        "count": count,
+                    }
+                    for (stage, forward_mode, call_site), count in (
+                        self._syncs.most_common(_MAX_CALL_SITES)
+                    )
+                ],
+            },
+        )
+        self._syncs.clear()
+        self._launched_batches.clear()
+        self._last_dump_time = now

+"""SchedulerHostSyncLogger counts torch sync-debug reports by scheduler stage,
+forward mode and call site, and dumps them with the launched batches. The
+scheduler calls its launch and result hooks once per step."""
+
+import unittest
+import warnings
+from collections import Counter
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import Mock, call, patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import Scheduler
+from sglang.srt.managers.utils import GenerationBatchResult
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_mode import ForwardMode
+from sglang.srt.observability.scheduler_stage_metrics import (
+    SCHEDULER_STAGE_GET_NEXT_BATCH,
+    SCHEDULER_STAGE_PROCESS_BATCH_RESULT,
+    SCHEDULER_STAGE_RUN_BATCH,
+    SchedulerStageMetricsRecorder,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils import scheduler_host_sync_logger as host_sync_module
+from sglang.srt.utils.scheduler_host_sync_logger import SchedulerHostSyncLogger
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+_SYNC_MESSAGE = "called a synchronizing CUDA operation"
+
+
+def _batch(mode: str):
+    return SimpleNamespace(forward_mode=SimpleNamespace(name=mode))
+
+
+def _issue_sync():
+    warnings.warn(_SYNC_MESSAGE, UserWarning)
+
+
+class TestSchedulerHostSyncLogger(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self._warnings = warnings.catch_warnings()
+        self._warnings.__enter__()
+        self._debug_mode = patch.object(torch.cuda, "set_sync_debug_mode")
+        self.set_sync_debug_mode = self._debug_mode.start()
+        self.recorder = SchedulerStageMetricsRecorder(enabled=True)
+        self.recorder.start(wall_ns=0)
+        self.records = []
+        self._log_json = patch.object(
+            host_sync_module,
+            "log_json",
+            side_effect=lambda loggers, event, data: self.records.append((event, data)),
+        )
+        self._log_json.start()
+        self.logger = SchedulerHostSyncLogger(
+            targets=["stdout"], dump_interval=0.0, stage_recorder=self.recorder
+        )
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        self._log_json.stop()
+        self._debug_mode.stop()
+        self._warnings.__exit__(None, None, None)
+
+    def test_maybe_create(self):
+        self.assertIsNone(
+            SchedulerHostSyncLogger.maybe_create(
+                enable_metrics=True, stage_recorder=self.recorder
+            )
+        )
+        with envs.SGLANG_LOG_SCHEDULER_HOST_SYNCS_TARGET.override("stdout"):
+            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                SchedulerHostSyncLogger.maybe_create(
+                    enable_metrics=False, stage_recorder=self.recorder
+                )
+            logger = SchedulerHostSyncLogger.maybe_create(
+                enable_metrics=True, stage_recorder=self.recorder
+            )
+        self.assertIsInstance(logger, SchedulerHostSyncLogger)
+        self.set_sync_debug_mode.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_counts_by_stage_mode_and_call_site(self):
+        with self.recorder.record(SCHEDULER_STAGE_RUN_BATCH):
+            self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+            _issue_sync()
+            _issue_sync()
+        self.set_sync_debug_mode.assert_called_once_with("warn")
+        with self.recorder.record(SCHEDULER_STAGE_GET_NEXT_BATCH):
+            _issue_sync()
+        with self.recorder.record(SCHEDULER_STAGE_PROCESS_BATCH_RESULT):
+            self.logger.on_step_result(_batch("EXTEND"))
+            _issue_sync()
+        self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+
+        self.assertEqual(len(self.records), 1)
+        event, data = self.records[0]
+        self.assertEqual(event, "scheduler.host_syncs")
+        self.assertEqual(data["launched_batches"], {"decode": 1})
+        self.assertEqual(data["total_syncs"], 4)
+        counts = Counter()
+        for sync in data["syncs"]:
+            counts[sync["stage"], sync["forward_mode"]] += sync["count"]
+        self.assertEqual(
+            counts,
+            {
+                (SCHEDULER_STAGE_RUN_BATCH, "decode"): 2,
+                (SCHEDULER_STAGE_GET_NEXT_BATCH, ""): 1,
+                (SCHEDULER_STAGE_PROCESS_BATCH_RESULT, "extend"): 1,
+            },
+        )
+        for sync in data["syncs"]:
+            innermost = sync["call_site"].split(" <- ")[0]
+            self.assertTrue(innermost.endswith(" _issue_sync"), innermost)
+
+    def test_window_is_cleared_after_dump(self):
+        with self.recorder.record(SCHEDULER_STAGE_RUN_BATCH):
+            self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("EXTEND"))
+            _issue_sync()
+        self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+        self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+        self.assertEqual([data["total_syncs"] for _, data in self.records], [1, 0])
+        self.assertEqual(self.records[1][1]["launched_batches"], {"decode": 1})
+
+    def test_other_warnings_pass_through(self):
+        shown = []
+        warnings.showwarning = lambda message, *args, **kwargs: shown.append(
+            str(message)
+        )
+        self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+        warnings.warn("unrelated", UserWarning)
+        self.assertEqual(shown, ["unrelated"])
+        self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+        self.assertEqual(self.records[0][1]["total_syncs"], 0)
+
+    def test_warns_once_when_hook_is_replaced(self):
+        self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+        warnings.showwarning = lambda *args, **kwargs: None
+        with self.assertLogs(host_sync_module.logger, level="WARNING") as logs:
+            self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+            self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+        self.assertEqual(len(logs.records), 1)
+        self.assertIn("no longer counted", logs.output[0])
+
+    @unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "needs a CUDA device")
+    def test_counts_real_device_read(self):
+        self._debug_mode.stop()
+        previous_mode = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
+        try:
+            x = torch.ones(4, device="cuda")
+            with self.recorder.record(SCHEDULER_STAGE_RUN_BATCH):
+                self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+                x.sum().item()
+            self.logger.on_step_launch(_batch("DECODE"))
+        finally:
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(previous_mode)
+            self._debug_mode.start()
+        (sync,) = self.records[0][1]["syncs"]
+        self.assertEqual(sync["stage"], SCHEDULER_STAGE_RUN_BATCH)
+        self.assertIn("test_counts_real_device_read", sync["call_site"])
+
+
+class TestSchedulerCallsHostSyncLogger(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_launch_and_result_hooks_run_once_per_step(self):
+        host_sync_logger = Mock(spec=["on_step_launch", "on_step_result"])
+        scheduler = Scheduler.__new__(Scheduler)
+        scheduler.metrics_reporter = Mock(
+            spec=[
+                "record_scheduler_active",
+                "log_batch_result_stats",
+                "update_device_timer",
+            ]
+        )
+        scheduler.metrics_reporter.scheduler_host_sync_logger = host_sync_logger
+        scheduler.scheduler_stage_metrics = None
+        scheduler.forward_ct = 0
+        scheduler._sched_idled = False
+        scheduler.processed_tokens_counter = 0
+        scheduler.scripted_scheduler_hook = None
+        scheduler.dllm_config = None
+        scheduler.enable_fpm = False
+        # The rest of a step's bookkeeping is out of scope here.
+        for name in (
+            "profiler_manager",
+            "invariant_checker",
+            "deferred_responses",
+            "publish_load_snapshot",
+            "load_publisher",
+            "load_inquirer",
+            "batch_result_processor",
+            "tree_cache",
+            "_on_step_processed",
+            "_record_step_counters",
+            "_maybe_clear_mm_inputs",
+            "maybe_send_health_check_signal",
+        ):
+            setattr(scheduler, name, Mock())
+
+        batches = [
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                reqs=[],
+                extend_num_tokens=0,
+                forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE,
+                add_inflight_step=Mock(),
+            )
+            for _ in range(2)
+        ]
+        for batch in batches:
+            Scheduler._on_step_launch(scheduler, batch)
+            Scheduler.process_batch_result(scheduler, batch, GenerationBatchResult())
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            host_sync_logger.mock_calls,
+            [
+                call.on_step_launch(batches[0]),
+                call.on_step_result(batches[0]),
+                call.on_step_launch(batches[1]),
+                call.on_step_result(batches[1]),
+            ],
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
